Round 8

2026-08-08 — round 8

All five pieces are now 68-73, mean delta +4.8, and perf recovered while five builders each added structure: draw calls 123 -> 113, triangles 218k -> 203k, worst-case JS frame 7.3 -> 2.4 ms. Making the budget a standing constraint on every builder rather than one agent's task worked on its first outing. Two findings outrank the scores. (1) THE SILHOUETTE METRIC IS INVALID, not merely noisy: `separation` divides by within-species pose variance, so it is maximised by a smooth mirror-symmetric body and is actively PAID FOR by deleting appendages. The builder duly tucked the strawberry calyx inside the waist to clear the gate, and the shipped silhouette lost its only outline cue — five of six fruit now read as featureless ovals. The frozen suite fixed reproducibility; this is validity, and a metric that rewards the opposite of the goal is worse than no metric. (2) THE ENTIRE FLESH DELIVERABLE IS OFF ON THE SHIPPING CONFIGURATION: fleshCells is gated behind pxFade(c, 3.4), and portrait renders the cut face at 0.745x linear, pushing fwidth past the edge. Desktop gained flesh R 131.0 -> 150.6; portrait gained 93.8 -> 96.3, and its G/R went the WRONG way. Third portrait-only defect found so far.

2026-08-08 — round 7

Every piece is now above 60 and silhouette reached 70; mean delta +4.8. Perf regressed as five builders each added structure and only one owned the budget: draw calls 88 -> 123 against a bar of 120, worst-case JS frame 3.4 -> 7.3 ms.

Round 6

2026-08-08 — round 6 (frozen probes)

FOUR PIECES CROSSED 60 for the first time and the deceleration reversed: mean delta +4.4 against round 5's +2.4. Freezing the measurement layer is the likeliest cause — three of this round's briefs started from CORRECTED baselines (materials was told it sat at 5.2% clipped, not the 14.07% its critic had reported), so builders chased real defects instead of instrument artefacts. The perf brief landed hard: draw calls 129 -> 88 against a bar of 120, triangles 216k -> 164k, worst-case JS frame 7.7 ms -> 3.4 ms. The lens fix was one boolean — the streak stops being a decal and writes depth — because post-processing cannot recover a depth that was never written, so opt-in was always the wrong structure. That change exposed two bugs that would have made the entire round worthless on an actual phone: the streak length and the CoC normalisation were both correct only in landscape, and portrait doubled the lens strength.

Round 5

2026-08-08 — round 5

Recovered round: the workflow died after the builders and integrator finished, and the stall daemon died with it — unnoticed for 11.7 hours, because the heartbeat file existed but nothing read it. Fixed: stallcheck now alarms on its own watch's staleness, proven by backdating the heartbeat. The critique was relaunched separately so no builder work was re-spent. Scores are plateauing (mean delta +2.4 against round 3's +10, nothing across 60) and the critics found why — THE MEASUREMENT LAYER IS NOW THE PROBLEM. Round 4

2026-08-07 — round 4

The exposure-owner experiment half worked. Serializing it did stop the cancellation, and the owner MEASURED the pipeline rather than deriving it — a ramp of Lambertian patches rendered through the real chain, fitted to a closed-form model at RMS 0.7-1.3/255, published as an albedo->display table. A contract fixes coordination; it does not by itself pick the right load case. Gains are also decelerating (+0 to +9, mean +4.2 against last round's +10) and three pieces are now blocked on files they do not own. The biggest of those was fixed by hand afterwards: director.js spawned uniform-random orientations, throwing away the silhouette geometry.js had authored — flagged by the critic three rounds running. Biasing the long axis toward the screen plane took the hero aspect from 1.000 to 0.784 and max protrusion from 18.3% to 28.3%.

Round 2

2026-08-07 — round 2 (WebGPURenderer + TSL)

Migrated to WebGPURenderer + TSL. The workflow itself died mid-round — all six agents finished their edits then expired on terminal API errors, and the pipeline hung ~12h waiting on one that never returned; the work was recovered from disk and integrated by hand. Every piece moved except the one that mattered most. Measured wins: the round-1 frame flood is gone (idle corners 177/147 -> ~0, blown pixels 1.91% -> 0.27% against the plate's 0.115%), and the flesh now has a real pale pith band at 5.3x the rind value where round 1 had none at all. The juice scored 0 delta: the fast-flick and slow-cleave frames measure as the same fluid in kind, and the critic found why — the fat juice-tinted spray budget GROWS with stroke speed, the exact inverse of the intent. Hero framing was fixed by hand afterwards: 30.0% -> 39.4% of frame height.

Round 1

2026-08-06 — round 1 (WebGL/GLSL)

Five builders rewrote lighting, materials, geometry, cut faces and juice; five independent critics blind-scored the real frames against the plate with pixel measurements. Net result: only juice improved. Overall composition got WORSE, because stage.js added a warm blade-flare streak whose broad haze lobe floods the entire frame — corner luminance 178 against the plate's 5. That is a good outcome for the loop: the critics caught a regression the builder was proud of, with numbers. Deep diagnoses landed on every piece and all of them port to TSL even though the GLSL does not. Harness was hardened before this ran: render at 0.5 scale, every await bounded, hard watchdog. Full run, zero errors, slowest beat 5.4s.

Round 0

2026-08-06 — baseline

End-to-end skeleton stood up by hand: real mesh slicing with generated cut faces, procedural fruit materials, GPU-analytic juice, blade ribbon, ballistic director, slow-mo reward, procedural audio, adaptive quality tiers, and a deterministic virtual-clock screenshot harness. Two real bugs found and fixed during bring-up: a negative first-frame delta permanently poisoning the fixed-step accumulator, and an uninitialised particle ring-buffer head that silently discarded every juice emission. Scores below are my own honest read against the bar, before any critic has looked.
